text:
alex: Quick sync — we're about to roll a staged exposure for the new routing policy that prefers low-latency variants per region/customer slice. Need input on scoping to customer tiers + model-variant fallback when latencies spike. TL;DR: how do we wire quotas, console exposure reporting, and safe fallback semantics? :thinking:

maria: Nice. Do we have a proposed config shape? I want anything that touches quotas to be explicit so Billing isn't surprised.

jon: Proposal sketch I shared in my draft PR yesterday: add a 'rollout_scope' field to RoutingPolicy and let RolloutService own exposure timers. Example snippet:
```json
{
  "routing_policy": "latency_aware",
  "rollout_scope": { "segments": ["enterprise","self-serve"], "percent_exposure": {"enterprise": 0.2, "self-serve": 0.05} },
  "fallback": { "type": "variant_swap", "variant": "quantized-v2", "threshold_ms": 250 }
}
```

alex: That looks reasonable. Question: should fallback be global or per-region/per-tier? I think per-tier, because enterprise gets higher SLO and different fallback tolerance.

kai: Agreed. Also console needs metrics by (region, tier, rollout_id). We should expose: route_exposure_pct, fallback_rate, p95_latency, cost_units_per_1k. Dashboards must have a selector for rollout_id and segment.

maria: Also add quota_shares per segment. If self-serve is 5% exposure but we've got 500 active requests, the quota must throttle gracefully instead of killing other segments. Something like: "quota_allocation": {"enterprise": 0.6, "self-serve": 0.3, "internal": 0.1}.

jon: Implementation debate: change RoutingPolicy proto to include rollout metadata vs a separate RolloutDescriptor object referenced by routing config. If we extend RoutingPolicy we risk bloat and breaking existing clients. I'm leaning to a lightweight RolloutDescriptor with id + version that controllers can reference.

sophie: For validation and auditing, the console's rollout UI should show expected vs observed exposure and highlight drift. Also add a synthetic-test-bucket to route a fixed set of test tokens so we can verify quantized-variant behavior without affecting real customers. Use header x-rollout-test: true to tag.

alex: Good point. We can create a 'play' segment that maps to a tenant list and always gets 0.5% traffic. That helps regression detection.

kai: Telemetry specifics: we need these metric tags - {route_id, rollout_id, segment, region, model_variant}. Track counters: requests_total, fallbacks_total, errors_total. Track histograms for latency and token_cost. Also log a sample of KV cache hit/miss correlated with fallback events.

maria: How do we present quotas in Console? Per-tenant quota_remaining, plus a global view. If fallback to cheaper variant increases cost savings, show cost delta estimate.

jon: API change checklist: 1) Add RolloutDescriptor resource, 2) Add binding between RoutingPolicy and RolloutDescriptor, 3) Add per-segment quota metadata, 4) Ensure backward-compatible defaults (no rollout => current behavior). Any objections?

alex: No objections. Need to decide whether fallback triggers are absolute latency thresholds or adaptive (percentile-based). Adaptive is nicer but harder to reason about.

kai: I'd vote for hybrid: percentile-based within the segment (p95 > X ms) OR absolute error spike > Y% within window. That covers noisy baselines.

sophie: UX note: rollout creation flow should force you to set fallback semantics and a rollback threshold. Don't let teams forget to configure those. Also expose a one-click rollback in the top-right of the rollout panel. :rocket:

maria: Ops concern — if fallback swaps model variant, we must ensure KV cache compatibility and warm-up plan. Otherwise we might cause a huge latency spike on swap. Document warm-up steps in rollout playbook.

jon: On the implementation side, we should treat fallback as a 'soft swap' first: route 10% traffic to fallback variant to warm caches, monitor, then ramp. That should be a built-in policy.

sre-bot: Reminder: any rollout that spans regions must be rate-limited by cross-region egress and have a circuit-breaker for region-level failure. Default fail-mode: isolate region and redirect to nearest healthy region's fallback variant.

alex: Good. Action items: jon - flesh PR + RolloutDescriptor proto; kai - telemetry + dashboard fields; maria - quota UI mockups and billing impact calc; sophie - UX flow + rollback button; I'll draft rollout playbook for warm-up and rollback. We'll loop infra for validation.

deploy-bot: Deployment window reserved 2026-03-20 03:00 UTC for rollout infra changes. Please add any migration tasks to the deploy checklist.

alex: Thanks everyone. I'll ping again once PR is up. :thumbsup:
